issue.title: Inconsistent error code conversion with gRPC cpp

repository.name: grpc-java
repository.description: The Java gRPC implementation. HTTP/2 based RPC

issue.body:
Please answer these questions before submitting your issue.

### What version of gRPC are you using?
v1.21.0

### What did you expect to see?
The HTTP to gRPC status code conversion is not consistent between Java & C++ implementations.
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/src/core/lib/transport/status_conversion.cc#L82
https://github.com/grpc/grpc-java/blame/master/core/src/main/java/io/grpc/internal/GrpcUtil.java#L305

As https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/issues/4735#issuecomment-432056484 mentioned, gRPC C Core maps 429 to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED but Java maps 429 to UNAVAILABLE.

issue.body:
statuscodes.md is one of the top search results for "grpc status codes",
right behind codes.proto. Since this is a landing page for many people*,
and since the title and description of this page purports to be the
generic status codes documentation page, it seems like a good idea to define
terms before using them.

\* Many people who are new to grpc/protobuf, for example, will be more
accustomed to and choose markdown files over .proto files.

issue.body:
The HTTP status codes are more for REST; they don't work with gRPC. We
shouldn't be encouraging them and they are confusing when you compare
them to doc/http-grpc-status-mapping.md .

-------

As brought to my attention by grpc/grpc-java#5916 (which was re-filed as #19094). This partially reverts #18003, but I don't think it impacts the original goal of that PR.

CC @jadekler, @sheenaqotj

body: @ejona86 Have the inconsistencies been resolved with your latest PR?
The doc is fixed. But the C core implementation https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/v1.23.0/src/core/lib/transport/status_conversion.cc#L82 is still wrong, there shouldn't be such conversion.
Yeah, the doc inconsistencies are fixed. But I've not touched status_conversion.cc
